ch2_p3_ipw_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Survey Non-Response and IPW Debiasing Workbench! Adjust the response rate and respondent mean sliders. Notice how the non-response bias formula accurately captures the distortion, and observe how Inverse Propensity Weighting restores the true mean.

ch2_p3_ipw_sim_duo.text: Look at that, Nova! When I pull response rate down to twenty percent with an eighty-five respondent mean and forty-five non-respondent mean, the unweighted bias shoots up to plus 3.2 points! That's a massive distortion on a ten-point scale!

ch2_p3_chk1_solo.text: Active Checkpoint 1: A customer survey of ten thousand users achieves a twenty percent response rate. Respondent mean is 8.5 out of 10. A follow-up phone audit reveals non-respondent mean is 4.5. Calculate true satisfaction and non-response bias.

ch2_p3_chk1_duo.text: Let us calculate: twenty percent times 8.5 plus eighty percent times 4.5... That gives 1.70 plus 3.60, which equals 5.30! And 8.5 minus 5.30 equals plus 3.20 points! Let's see if our students get it right!

ch2_p3_chk1_feedback_correct.text: Outstanding! By the non-response theorem: true satisfaction Y bar equals 0.20 times 8.5 plus 0.80 times 4.5, which equals 5.30. Therefore, non-response bias equals 8.50 minus 5.30, or exactly plus 3.20 points! The naive survey grossly overestimates customer satisfaction.

ch2_p3_chk1_feedback_incorrect.text: Not quite. Remember that true population mean is a convex combination: 0.20 times 8.5 plus 0.80 times 4.5 equals 5.30. Subtracting 5.30 from 8.50 yields a bias of plus 3.20 points.

ch2_p3_scraping_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Web Scraping Rate Limiter and Structural Drift Simulator! Adjust crawl delay, worker concurrency, and DOM mutation rate. Observe how exceeding maximum allowable requests per second violates RFC 9309 politeness, and watch the Jaccard distance trip the circuit breaker.

ch2_p3_scraping_sim_duo.text: Watch this, Nova! Crawl-delay is 0.5 seconds, meaning max RPS is 2.0. But when I push concurrent workers to 6, actual RPS hits 6.0 and the DoS safety badge flashes critical red! And pushing mutation rate to 45% trips the Jaccard circuit breaker!

ch2_p3_chk2_solo.text: Active Checkpoint 2: A remote website publishes a robots.txt file with Crawl-delay: 0.5. What is the maximum permissible request rate per second across all concurrent threads? Select Option A, B, or C above me.

ch2_p3_chk2_duo.text: Remember the reciprocal rule: RPS max equals one divided by Crawl-delay. One divided by 0.5 seconds equals 2.0 requests per second! Let's challenge our engineers to pick the right option above us!

ch2_p3_chk2_feedback_correct.text: Precisely correct! The maximum permissible request rate is the reciprocal of the crawl delay: 1 divided by 0.5 seconds equals 2.0 requests per second. Exceeding this rate violates RFC 9309 etiquette and risks automated IP bans.

ch2_p3_chk2_feedback_incorrect.text: That is incorrect. Recall the reciprocal formula: RPS max equals 1 divided by Crawl-delay. One divided by 0.5 seconds equals 2.0 requests per second.
